newsitem.title: MONACO: ATHLETICS-IAAF UNIMPRESSED BY JOHNSON APPEAL BID.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-IAAF UNIMPRESSED BY JOHNSON APPEAL BID.

text.p: Ben Johnson's attempts to race competitively again were dismissed as "strange" by the International Amateur Athletic Federation on Thursday.

The 35-year-old Canadian sprinter, banned for life after a second positive drug test in 1993, was said by his manager Morris Chrobotek to have made a request this week for reinstatement, but IAAF spokesman Giorgio Reineri denied any formal application had been received.
"We have had an exchange of papers but we haven't received any official request from the Canadian federation," said Reineri, suggesting the athlete had little hope of a reprieve.

"Ben Johnson did not appeal when he was banned for life three years ago...it's a little strange to us that three years on he suddenly wants to do so. I don't know if there is any probability of him being reinstated."
Chrobotek, nevertheless, is still hopeful the former 100-metre world-record holder will be running internationally by the summer this year.

"The man has served his time, he has been rehabilitated," Chrobotek said on Wednesday. "What exactly is a lifetime ban?" he said. "If (a criminal) receives a lifetime sentence, is he ever let out (on parole)?
"With anything in life, the only time something is final is when you die."
He also claims that Johnson recently posted an electronically timed 100-metre mark of 9.93 seconds. That would represent the eighth-fastest time worldwide over that distance.

Donovan Bailey holds the 100-metre world record of 9.84 seconds. Johnson had a time of 9.79 seconds at the 1988 Olympics in Seoul but was stripped of that record and the Olympic gold medal after testing positive for anabolic steroids.
